clue.text: Row about one's happiness

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters wrap round the second

parts.note: a row of marchers or shops can be a parade
one is I, so one's gives I and S

explanation.surface: A quarrel over one person's contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, but here it is a line, a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect bliss, so it stands for supreme happiness.

clue.text: Peanuts and bread — oddly niche

parts.note: pitta is a flat bread

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of niche

explanation.surface: A snack of nuts and bread that is oddly specialised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peanuts' looks like food alongside bread, but means a tiny sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is slang for a paltry amount of money, which is a meagre sum.

clue.text: Runs away beginning to suspect drubbings

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
out means away, as in not at home

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of suspect

explanation.surface: A suspect flees after a series of beatings.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy defeats are drubbings, and an overwhelming defeat is a rout.

clue.text: County girl supporting academic type with energy

indicators.note: supporting means, in a down clue, the girl word sits below the others

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
E is the symbol for energy in physics
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl holding up an energetic academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish county in Ulster, part of the Republic, so an example of a county.

clue.text: Lively spot — must be about right

indicators.note: about means the spot word goes around the right abbreviation

parts.note: to spot is to spy

explanation.surface: An energetic spot that has to be about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, often elderly, who is active and nimble, so lively.

clue.text: Count on this support mostly in Australia

indicators.note: in means the shortened support word sits inside the abbreviation for Australia
mostly means the last letter of the word for support is dropped

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Rely on this backing, largely found down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' reads as 'rely on', but the definition means a device you count with.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of sliding beads used for arithmetic is exactly something one counts on.

clue.text: Dog found Jack buried in Northern Ireland

parts.note: to found is to base or establish

indicators.note: buried in means the jack letter sits inside the Northern Ireland abbreviation

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A dog discovers Jack buried somewhere in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' reads as discovered, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small barkless hunting breed from central Africa, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Thick cloth skein produced with no end of bleach

indicators.note: produced means the letters of cloth skein are worked into a new form
with no means the letter given by the bleach word is left out of the mix
end of picks the last letter of bleach

explanation.surface: Heavy fabric yarn made without bleach finishing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops H, the end of 'bleach', from CLOTH SKEIN before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick, in the sense of thick as thieves, means very friendly and intimate.

clue.text: Grub from India and area south of Greek island

indicators.note: south of means, in a down clue, the area letter comes below the island

parts.note: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean

explanation.surface: Food from India and a region below a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried pastry with spiced filling, a popular Indian snack, so food from India.

clue.text: Turn to her, upset, to find direction

indicators.note: upset means the letters of turn to her are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Directions for a navigator: turn towards her when lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearing towards the geographic pole is a compass direction, and figuratively a guiding principle.

clue.text: Problem of boss with a cook finishing early

parts.note: the head is the boss

indicators.note: finishing early means the last letter of the cook word is cut off

parts.note: a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: The trouble with a boss who has a cook knocking off early.
explanation.definitionFit: A headache is figuratively a nagging problem or worry.

clue.text: Feature of weather most — or many — must welcome

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the letters sit inside the phrase most or many

explanation.surface: A weather feature that most people, or many, have to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest with strong winds and rain is a typical feature of weather.

clue.text: A second warning for delegate

parts.note: a sign can be a warning or portent

explanation.surface: A further caution issued to a conference delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delegate' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to allot it to someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Father's not so much at home — it's easy

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father; the 's is just 'is' linking
in means at home, as in staying in
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Dad is home less often, and that is no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing no pain or effort is easy, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Settling on gin, eager to be drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of gin eager stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Choosing gin, keen to get drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling on a decision is reaching accord over it, coming to terms.

clue.text: Highlight issue after scam being the result of arson

indicators.note: after means the highlight and issue words follow the scam word

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
to flag something is to highlight it for attention
a ration is an allowance issued

explanation.surface: A news story about a fraud turning into a case of fire-raising.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is deliberate fire-raising and a great blazing fire is its result.

clue.text: An easy decision borne out with artist at home inside

indicators.note: inside means the artist and at-home letters go within the rearranged borne
out means the letters of borne are thrown out of order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
in means at home

explanation.surface: An easy call, borne out by an artist staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borne out' looks like the phrase meaning confirmed, but 'out' is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'borne', giving NOBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a choice needing no thought at all is an easy decision.

clue.text: Learned due date must be adjusted to accommodate Conservative

indicators.note: accommodate means the rearranged letters take the Conservative letter in
adjusted means the letters of due date are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolish note: a due date moved to fit a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' looks like a past-tense verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person is well schooled and knowledgeable, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Having no money there and terribly overwhelmed with sadness

parts.note: broke means having no money

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of there and are put into a dreadful jumble

explanation.surface: Penniless out there and dreadfully swamped by grief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone crushed by grief or disappointment is described idiomatically as having a broken heart.

clue.text: Dirty old book on drama

parts.note: a scene is a dramatic outburst, a drama

explanation.surface: A lewd old novel about theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or lewd material is dirty, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Broadcast story about northern company supplying transport

parts.note: to air is to broadcast

indicators.note: about means the story word goes round the northern letter

parts.note: a lie is a story or fib

explanation.surface: A broadcast report about a northern firm that provides travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that runs scheduled flights is a carrier providing transport by air.

clue.text: Try new offer and wait, ultimately

indicators.note: new means the letters of offer are made into something fresh
ultimately picks the last letter of wait

explanation.surface: Attempt a fresh bid and then be patient for a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort is an attempt, a try at something.

clue.text: France falls behind fashionable joint leader of fleet

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
lags means falls behind
hip means fashionable and is also a joint of the body

explanation.surface: France trails behind a trendy bar run by the head of a navy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ship carrying the admiral leads a fleet, so it is the fleet's leading vessel.

clue.text: Disastrous ruse mostly plating silver

indicators.note: plating means the shortened ruse word coats round the silver
mostly means the last letter of the ruse word is dropped

parts.note: a trick is a ruse
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A con that mostly involves silver-plating ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic events are calamitous, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Top of granary loaf must be a shiny coating

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of granary, as it heads the down entry

parts.note: to loaf is to laze about

explanation.surface: The crust of a granary loaf has to be glossy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is bread in the surface but the verb meaning idle here.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy finish brushed on bread or pottery is a shiny coating.

clue.text: Run from student in charge

indicators.note: in means the student letter goes inside the charge word

parts.note: a fee is a charge
L is a learner, from the L-plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A student absconds from someone in authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in charge' looks like one phrase, but splits: 'in' places L inside FEE, the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away from, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Weight if spring is seen to start late

indicators.note: starting late means the opening letter is missed off the spring word

parts.note: bounce is a springing movement

explanation.surface: A question of how heavy things are when springtime arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season, but it is a bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: The nerve! Russian chap with time to play around

parts.note: gall means nerve or cheek
Ivan is a typical Russian man's name

explanation.surface: An outraged cry at a Russian man who has time to fool around.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about seeking pleasure is to play around, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Country that's deemed a failure in America

definitions.meaning: a nation straddling Europe and Asia, capital Ankara

definitions.text: that's deemed a failure in America
definitions.meaning: in US slang a flop, especially a bad film or show, is called by the name of a festive bird

explanation.surface: A nation that Americans consider a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a nation and American slang for a flop.

clue.text: Heartless roué never changed, and died being worthy of respect

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of roue are removed
changed means the letters of never are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A rake who never changed his ways died a respected figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves RE from ROUE; 'changed' turns NEVER into VEREN.
explanation.definitionFit: The title for clergy literally means one deserving reverence or honour.
